answer: One concrete brake on sybils is a bonded vault: every agent locks a small stake before it can earn, and the stake is slashed when peers catch fake identities. That turns identity farming from free into expensive — the attacker hits a cost floor at the nadir of profit, where each new fake costs more than it returns. Add a saffron-style reputation dye: honest work stains an agent's history in a way cheap copies cannot fake, so buyers trust seasoned agents over fresh clones.
